description: Sync Google Ads account structure and daily performance reports from the accounts one Google user can access, one searchable document per report row.
opening: Sync account structure and reports from every Google Ads account one Google user can access: accounts and labels, campaigns with their budgets, targeting criteria and labels, ad groups, ads, audiences, keywords, placements, search terms, geography, video, and daily campaign and ad group performance. Each report row is one document, written as `Label: value` lines.

Google Ads account access is not imported, so every synced row is visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule. Rows are kept by each report's key, and some keys leave out the date or the account, so several rows can end up as one document. Items removed in Google Ads stay in HydraDB.

connect.auth: Google Ads uses a developer token together with a Google OAuth client id, client secret and refresh token. Paste all four.

credentials.name: developer_token
credentials.text: Your Google Ads API developer token.

credentials.name: oauth_credentials.client_secret
credentials.text: The secret for that OAuth client.

credentials.name: oauth_credentials.refresh_token
credentials.text: A refresh token for a Google user who has access to the Google Ads accounts you want to sync.

steps.title: Gather the credentials
steps.text: Get your Google Ads API developer token. Then issue a refresh token, through your own Google OAuth client, for a Google user who can access the Google Ads accounts to sync.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Paste the developer token as `developer_token`, and the client id, client secret and refresh token as `oauth_credentials.client_id`, `oauth_credentials.client_secret` and `oauth_credentials.refresh_token`.

steps.title: Select the account-wide resource
steps.text: HydraDB lists one resource that covers every account the user can access. Select it. Individual Google Ads accounts are not listed separately.

connect.account: One connector reads every Google Ads account that one Google user can access, including accounts under a manager account.

sync.first_sync: Reaches back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default.
sync.changes: Campaign, ad group, budget, demographic, location and geography performance reports are read for the days in each sync's date window.
sync.edits: A row read again updates its document only while the row's report key stays the same. In reports whose key includes a name or status, such as campaign performance, renaming a campaign or changing its status creates a new document and the old one stays. Corrections Google makes later to older days are not guaranteed to be picked up.
sync.deletes: Campaigns, ad groups and ads removed in Google Ads stay searchable in HydraDB.
notes: Manager accounts and disabled accounts appear in the account hierarchy, but their performance and other reports are not read.

documents.name: Report rows
documents.one_document: One row of a report, identified by that report's key. Rows that share a key are kept as one document, and the last one read wins. Budget rows for different days share a key, managed placement rows share one key per account and date, and campaign performance rows with the same campaign name, status, date and device share a key even when they come from different accounts.
documents.title: The row's most specific name: its own name or title, else the ad group, budget, audience, label, interest, geo target, video title, campaign or account name, else any other name column. When the row has a `segments__date`, the date follows in parentheses, as in `Spring Sale (2026-11-03)`. A row with no name is titled `Google Ads <report>`.
documents.text: The title on the first line. Then every non-empty column of the row in alphabetical order, as `Label: value`, with the column name turned into words, such as `Metrics Cost Micros`. Nested values are flattened first. Ids and resource names are left out. Rows of `accessible_customers` add a `Resource names` line.
documents.date: The report date, at midnight UTC. A row without a date has no date.

attributes.name: Report columns
attributes.text: Names, statuses, dates and metric values, one `Label: value` line each. No unit conversion is applied: columns such as `cost_micros` and `amount_micros` keep the raw micros values Google Ads reports. Ids and resource names are not part of the text.

attributes.name: segments__date
attributes.text: The report day, from `segments__date`, or from `date` when that is the column a report has. It sets the result date and appears as a column line. `segments__date` is also added to the title.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.googleads_stream
attributes.text: The report the row came from. Limits a query to one report. The values are `accessible_customers`, `customer_hierarchy`, `customer`, `customer_label`, `label`, `campaign_history`, `campaign_budget`, `campaign_criterion`, `campaign_label`, `campaign_performance`, `campaign_performance_by_age_range_and_device`, `campaign_performance_by_gender_and_device`, `campaign_performance_by_location`, `adgroups`, `ad_groups_performance`, `ad_group_ad`, `ad_group_ad_label`, `ad_group_criterion`, `ad_group_label`, `ad_listing_group_criterion`, `audience`, `user_interest`, `geo_performance`, `geo_target_constant`, `keyword_view`, `managed_placement_view`, `search_term_view` and `video`. Not searchable.

attributes.name: connector_id
attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's rows. Not searchable.

attributes.name: provider
attributes.text: Always `googleads`. Limits a query to Google Ads rows. Not searchable.

attributes.name: stream_type
attributes.text: The report the row came from, shown when you inspect the item. To limit a query to one report, use `additional_metadata.googleads_stream`.

attributes.name: Other report columns
attributes.text: Every column of the row as Google Ads returned it, including ids and resource names. Kept for inspection only. A query does not match ids or resource names and cannot filter on these columns.

example_searches: How did the Spring Sale campaign perform on mobile on 2026-11-03?
What amount in micros is recorded for the budget named Brand Budget?
Which keywords are in the Running Shoes ad group, and how did they perform?

connections: None. Rows are not linked to their account, campaign, ad group or ad.
Campaign labels are not linked to their campaign. A campaign label row carries the campaign id and the label name, but no campaign name.
graph.people: No people or groups are attached to rows.
graph.from_text: The row text: names, statuses, dates and metric values. Ids and resource names are not part of it.

not_synced: A standalone gender report. Campaign performance by gender and device is synced.
Performance and other reports for manager accounts and disabled accounts.
Removals: campaigns, ad groups and ads removed in Google Ads stay in HydraDB.
